assignedReviews.card_evidence: A whale shark can grow about 12 to 18 meters long

assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a measurement in meters but does not describe or demonstrate a science process skill such as observing, predicting, or measuring.

copy.en: A whale shark can grow about 12 to 18 meters long — longer than a bus!
copy.tl: Ang butanding ay maaaring umabot sa 12 hanggang 18 metro ang haba — mas mahaba pa sa isang bus!
copy.bis: Ang tuki makaabot ug 12 ngadto sa 18 ka metro ang gitas-on — mas taas pa sa usa ka bus!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: makes sounds so low that people can barely hear them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a characteristic of a blue whale's sound (very low, barely audible) but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It shares the topic of sound but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: makes sounds so low that people can barely hear them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sound but does not identify sources and uses of sound energy at school, home, or in the local community. A blue whale's low sound is not an everyday local source/use, so the card is only related to the broad subject of sound.

copy.en:
What does the biggest animal on Earth sound like?

The blue whale, the largest animal on Earth, makes sounds so low that people can barely hear them — very different from the higher melody of the humpback whale!
copy.tl:
Anong tunog ang ginagawa ng pinakamalaking hayop sa mundo?

Ang blue whale, ang pinakamalaking hayop sa mundo, ay gumagawa ng napakababang tunog na halos hindi marinig ng tao — ibang-iba ito sa mas mataas na himig ng humpback!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga tingog ang gihimo sa pinakadako nga hayop sa kalibotan?

Ang blue whale, ang pinakadako nga hayop sa kalibotan, naghimo og ubos kaayo nga tingog nga halos dili madungog sa tawo — lahi kaayo kini sa mas taas nga huni sa humpback!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it moves air around inside its body near its throat to make sounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how a whale produces sound by moving air, but the competency focuses on everyday situations such as ringing a bell or hearing noises. The whale example is not an everyday situation and does not directly support the stated skill of exploring sound in everyday contexts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A whale doesn't use its mouth to sing—it moves air around inside its body near its throat to make sounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about observing and describing outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and gathering food. The card discusses internal air movement for sound production, not outer body parts or their roles in movement/feeding. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
How does a whale sing without vocal cords?

A whale doesn't use its mouth to sing—it moves air around inside its body near its throat to make sounds, almost like whistling or humming.
copy.tl:
Paano kumakanta ang balyena kahit hindi gumagamit ng bibig?

Hindi gumagamit ng bibig ang balyena para kumanta—pinapadaan nila ang hangin sa loob ng katawan, malapit sa lalamunan, kaya lumilikha ito ng tunog na parang sumisipol o humuhuni.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkanta sa balyena bisan wala magamit ang baba?

Wala mogamit ug baba ang balyena aron mokanta—gipaagi nila ang hangin sa sulod sa lawas, duol sa tutunlan, mao nga makahimo kini og tingog nga morag nagpasipol o naghuni.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: While traveling to warm waters to have their babies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions having babies but does not address the distinction between live birth and egg-laying groups, which is the core of G5-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: While traveling to warm waters to have their babies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on reproduction (having babies) but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a set; it is a specific behavioral fact about whales, not a general description of living things.

copy.en:
When do humpback whales sing the most?

While traveling to warm waters to have their babies — the singing seems to help them find a mate.
copy.tl:
Kailan pinakamadalas kumanta ang humpback whale?

Habang naglalakbay sila papunta sa mainit na tubig para magkaanak — parang bahagi ito ng paghahanap ng kapareha.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a labing kanunay mokanta ang humpback whale?

Samtang nagpanaw sila padulong sa init nga tubig aron manganak — morag bahin kini sa pagpangita og kapikas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound travels faster and farther through water than through air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sound transfer through water, but the competency targets everyday situations like a ringing bell or hearing noises. Whale song in the ocean is not an everyday situation for Grade 3, and the card does not explore how sound is made or transferred in common contexts.

copy.en:
Why can whales hear each other from far away?

Sound travels faster and farther through water than through air. So even when two whales are far apart in the ocean, they can still hear each other's songs.
copy.tl:
Bakit naririnig ng balyena ang kasama nito kahit malayo?

Mas mabilis at malayo ang lakbay ng tunog sa tubig kaysa sa hangin. Kaya kahit magkalayo ang dalawang balyena sa dagat, naririnig pa rin nila ang kanta ng isa't isa.
copy.bis:
Nganong madungog sa balyena ang kauban bisan layo?

Mas paspas ug mas layo ang panaw sa tingog sa tubig kaysa sa hangin. Mao nga bisan magkalayo ang duha ka balyena sa dagat, madungog gihapon nila ang kanta sa usag usa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A whale song has structure — small sounds join into 'phrases,' and the whale repeats these phrases to build a whole song
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the structural organization of whale songs, which is about sound as a communication phenomenon. G4-F-10 requires observing and identifying sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy in everyday settings. The card does not address sources of sound, uses of sound energy, or any school/home/community context, so it only shares the broad topic of sound.

copy.en: A whale song has structure — small sounds join into 'phrases,' and the whale repeats these phrases to build a whole song, like verses in a song.
copy.tl: May istruktura ang kanta ng balyena — pinagsasama ang maliliit na tunog para bumuo ng 'parirala,' at inuulit ito ng balyena para makabuo ng buong kanta.
copy.bis: Naay istruktura ang kanta sa balyena — gitipon ang gagmay nga tingog aron mahimong 'pulong,' ug gibalik-balik kini sa balyena aron mabuo ang tibuok kanta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound travels much farther in water than in air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of sound transfer (farther in water) but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations like ringing bells or hearing noises. It is a factual statement about sound propagation, not an everyday exploration or description of sound transfer.

copy.en: Sound travels much farther in water than in air, which is why whales can hear each other even when they are far apart.
copy.tl: Mas malayo ang nilalakbay ng tunog sa tubig kaysa sa hangin, kaya naririnig ng mga balyena ang isa't isa kahit magkalayo.
copy.bis: Ang tingog molakaw og mas layo sa tubig kaysa sa hangin, mao nga madunggan sa balyena ang usag usa bisan layo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A landform is a natural shape on Earth's surface! Cool examples include mountains, hills, plains, and valleys.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines landforms and gives examples, but does not identify local examples or describe how landforms influence non-living and living components, which are the core actions of the competency. It provides background knowledge only.

copy.en: A landform is a natural shape on Earth's surface! Cool examples include mountains, hills, plains, and valleys.
copy.tl: Ang anyong lupa ay mga natural na hugis sa ibabaw ng Earth! Kasama rito ang mga bundok, burol, kapatagan, at lambak.
copy.bis: Ang anyo sa yuta mao ang natural nga porma sa ibabaw sa kalibotan! Lakip niini ang bukid, bungtod, patag, ug walog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A valley is low land between mountains or hills
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a valley but does not identify local examples or describe how landforms influence living/non-living components, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: often carved out by a river over a long time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions river carving as a cause of valleys, which relates to erosion, but it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials, so it is not direct support.

copy.en:
Ever wonder what a valley is?

A valley is low land between mountains or hills, often carved out by a river over a long time!
copy.tl:
Napapaisip ka ba kung ano ang lambak?

Ang lambak ay mababang lupa sa pagitan ng mga bundok o burol, na kadalasang inukit ng ilog sa paglipas ng panahon!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba ka unsa ang walog?

Ang walog mao ang ubos nga yuta tunga sa mga bukid o bungtod, kasagaran gikalot sa suba sa paglabay sa panahon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ethnoastronomy studies how each culture understands the sky
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains cultural interpretations of star patterns (ethnoastronomy). G3-F-1 is about making objects move by natural causes or by people (pushing, pulling, rolling, carrying). There is no connection to force, motion, or moving objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the study of how cultures understand the sky
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains ethnoastronomy, a cultural interpretation of the sky. It contains no content about solubility, solutes, solvents, or factors affecting solubility. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's subject.

copy.en:
Why do people from different places see different pictures in the same stars?

Ethnoastronomy studies how each culture understands the sky in its own way, so the same stars can tell different stories!
copy.tl:
Bakit iba-iba ang nakikitang larawan ng mga tao sa iisang grupo ng bituin?

Pinag-aaralan ng ethnoastronomy kung paano nauunawaan ng bawat kultura ang langit sa sarili nilang paraan, kaya ang parehong bituin ay may iba't ibang kuwento!
copy.bis:
Ngano lain-lain man ang makita nga mga hulagway sa mga tawo sa samang grupo sa bituon?

Gitun-an sa ethnoastronomy kung giunsa pagsabot sa matag kultura ang langit sa ilang kaugalingong paagi, mao nga ang samang bituon adunay lain-laing mga sugilanon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A fossil is the preserved trace or remains of a plant or animal that lived long ago, kept safely inside rock!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines what a fossil is. It does not describe how fossils are used for dating the age of rocks and sediments, which is the core action of the competency. The definition is useful background but does not directly teach dating methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A fossil is the preserved trace or remains of a plant or animal that lived long ago, kept safely inside rock!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a basic definition of a fossil, which is background for understanding the geologic time scale, but it does not explain how the geologic time scale recounts Earth's history. No direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: A fossil is the preserved trace or remains of a plant or animal that lived long ago, kept safely inside rock!
copy.tl: Ang fossil ay ang naiwang bakas o labi ng halaman o hayop na matagal nang nabuhay, na napreserba sa loob ng bato!
copy.bis: Ang fossil mao ang nahibilin nga timaan o lawas sa tanom o hayop nga dugay nang nabuhi, nga natipigan sulod sa bato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A gemstone is a rare, beautiful mineral!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a gemstone as a mineral but does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. It shares the topic of minerals but provides no instructional support for the competency's specific skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A gemstone is a rare, beautiful mineral!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions minerals but does not involve observing, collecting, or comparing rocks by texture, color, or grain crystal size. It is only tangentially related to the broader rocks and minerals content.

copy.en: A gemstone is a rare, beautiful mineral! It gets cut and polished into gorgeous jewelry like diamond and ruby.
copy.tl: Ang gemstone ay isang bihira at magandang mineral! Pinuputol at pinakikintab ito para gawing magagandang alahas tulad ng diamond at ruby.
copy.bis: Ang gemstone usa ka talagsaon ug nindot nga mineral! Giputol ug gipasinaw kini aron himoong nindot nga alahas sama sa diamond ug ruby.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists use it to measure the massive distances between the stars.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a light-year as a unit of distance for measuring star distances. It does not support observing or describing the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars, which is the focus of G3-E-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists use it to measure the massive distances between the stars.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only introduces a distance unit used in astronomy. It does not describe the structure of the solar system, nor identify the names, main features, or composition of major celestial objects as required by G5-E-11.

copy.en: A light-year is the huge distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometers! Scientists use it to measure the massive distances between the stars.
copy.tl: Ang light-year ay ang napakalayong distansya na nilalakbay ng liwanag sa isang taon, mga 9.5 trillion kilometers! Ginagamit ito para sukatin ang distansya sa pagitan ng mga bituin.
copy.bis: Ang light-year mao ang dagkong gilay-on nga gibiyahe sa kahayag sulod sa usa ka tuig, mga 9.5 trillion kilometers! Gigamit kini aron sukoron ang gilay-on tali sa mga bituon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rock is a hard, natural solid that is made of one or more minerals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines what a rock is. It does not involve exploring, collecting, or comparing rock types by texture, color, or grain crystal size, so it is background knowledge rather than direct instruction for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rock is a hard, natural solid that is made of one or more minerals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a definition of one non-living thing (rock) but does not guide locating or describing different types of non-living things in the school environment. It is useful background but not direct support for the guided activity.

copy.en:
What exactly is a rock?

A rock is a hard, natural solid that is made of one or more minerals!
copy.tl:
Ano nga ba ang bato?

Ang bato ay isang matigas na natural na bagay na binubuo ng isa o higit pang mineral!
copy.bis:
Unsa man gyud ang bato?

Ang bato usa ka gahi nga natural nga butang nga hinimo gikan sa usa o daghang mineral!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rocket is a machine that burns fuel to create a powerful upward push
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a rocket's fuel-based propulsion, not the natural causes (wind, water) or human actions (pushing, pulling, rolling, carrying) that G3-F-1 asks students to explore and demonstrate. It shares the broad topic of moving objects but does not directly support the competency's specific actions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: create a powerful upward push
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that when any two objects interact, there are equal but opposite forces exerted between them, which is evident in many practical situations and applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a push but does not explain equal and opposite forces between interacting objects, which is the core of Newton's third law in G9-F-4. It does not teach the action-reaction principle or provide practical situations illustrating it.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: letting it leave Earth and travel into space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions space travel but does not explain how modern research uses telescopes, space probes, or other space technologies. It only states that a rocket can go into space, which is not the competency's focus on research technologies.

copy.en:
What is a rocket?

A rocket is a machine that burns fuel to create a powerful upward push, letting it leave Earth and travel into space!
copy.tl:
Ano ang rocket?

Ang rocket ay makina na sumusunog ng panggatong para gumawa ng malakas na pwersa pataas, kaya nakakalabas ito ng Earth papuntang kalawakan!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang rocket?

Ang rocket usa ka makina nga nagasunog og gasolina aron makahimo og kusog nga pwersa pataas, mao nga makagawas kini sa Earth padulong sa kawanangan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Limiting factors are environmental conditions or resources
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses population-limiting factors in ecology, with no mention of metals, their properties, or local community uses. It does not support identifying properties/uses of iron, gold, silver, or copper.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Limiting factors are environmental conditions or resources
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about ecological limiting factors, not about useful things made from non-living materials or the natural materials used. No connection to G3-E-2.

copy.en: Limiting factors are environmental conditions or resources, like food, water, and space, that restrict how large a population can grow.
copy.tl: Ang limiting factors ay mga kondisyon o resources sa kapaligiran, tulad ng pagkain, tubig, at space, na naglilimita kung gaano kalaki ang maaaring lumaking population.
copy.bis: Ang limiting factors mao ang mga kondisyon o resources sa kinaiyahan, sama sa pagkaon, tubig, ug space, nga naglimite kung unsa kadako ang mahimong population.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gears are toothed wheels on axles! Their teeth lock together to pass on the turning motion — just like on your bicycle!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines gears and gives a bicycle as an example, but it does not describe gears as a simple machine, nor does it provide examples and uses found at home, school, or community as required by the competency. The bicycle mention is a single use, not a description of uses or observation of simple machines.

copy.en:
What are gears and how do they work?

Gears are toothed wheels on axles! Their teeth lock together to pass on the turning motion — just like on your bicycle!
copy.tl:
Ano ang mga gear at paano sila gumagana?

Ang mga gear ay mga gulong na may ngipin sa ehe! Nagkakabit ang mga ngipin para maipasa ang ikot — parang sa bisikleta mo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mga gear ug unsaon nila pagtrabaho?

Ang mga gear mao mga ligid nga adunay ngipon sa aksis! Nagkabit ang mga ngipon aron mabalhin ang tuyok — sama sa imong bisikleta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The bigger the wheel compared to the axle, the greater the mechanical advantage!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a principle of the wheel and axle, a simple machine, but does not provide examples or uses found at home, school, or in the community as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The bigger the wheel compared to the axle, the greater the mechanical advantage!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card states an advantage of the wheel and axle but does not demonstrate through guided investigation, nor does it address limitations or the named simple machines (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys).

copy.en:
What happens when the wheel is much bigger than the axle?

The bigger the wheel compared to the axle, the greater the mechanical advantage! That means you need less force to turn it.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag mas malaki ang gulong kaysa ehe?

Kapag mas malaki ang gulong kumpara sa ehe, mas malaki ang mechanical advantage! Ibig sabihin, mas kaunting puwersa ang kailangan para paikutin ito.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung mas dako ang ligid kaysa aksis?

Kon mas dako ang ligid kumpara sa aksis, mas dako ang mechanical advantage! Buot ipasabot, gamay ra nga puwersa ang gikinahanglan aron tuyokon kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: use very long front legs to feel their way in the dark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: Long front legs used to feel in the dark is not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whip spiders live in Philippine caves and aren't true spiders — they have no venom or silk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Whip spider versus true spider is two invertebrate groups, not vertebrates versus invertebrates.

copy.en: Whip spiders live in Philippine caves and aren't true spiders — they have no venom or silk, and use very long front legs to feel their way in the dark.
copy.tl: Ang whip spiders ay nakatira sa mga kuweba ng Pilipinas at hindi talaga gagamba — walang sila lason o sutla, at ginagamit nila ang napakahabang harapang binti para pumalag sa dilim.
copy.bis: Ang whip spiders nagpuyo sa mga kuweba sa Pilipinas ug dili tinuod nga gagamba — walay hilo o sutla, ug gigamit nila ang taas kaayo nga unang tiil aron mabatian ang dalan sa ngitngit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a nearby jet plane reaches over 120 decibels—extremely loud!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of how objects can affect other objects even when they are not in contact with each other, such as magnets attracting other objects, light from the sun, and loud noises hurting our ears
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives decibel levels for a whisper and a jet plane, but it does not describe how sound affects other objects or ears without contact. It does not teach the non-contact effect concept (e.g., loud noises hurting ears).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A quiet whisper is only about 30 decibels, but a nearby jet plane reaches over 120 decibels
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides examples of sound levels, but it does not explain how sound is made or transferred. It lacks the mechanism or everyday transfer context required by the competency.

copy.en: A quiet whisper is only about 30 decibels, but a nearby jet plane reaches over 120 decibels—extremely loud!
copy.tl: Ang bulong ay mga 30 desibel lang, pero ang malapit na eroplanong jet ay umaabot ng higit 120 desibel—sobrang lakas!
copy.bis: Ang hagawhaw mga 30 desibel ra, apan ang duol nga jet nga ayroplano makaabot og kapin 120 desibel—sobra ka kusog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The word "dinosaur" was coined by English scientist Richard Owen!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a foreign scientist (Richard Owen) and a contribution (coining the word 'dinosaur'), but the competency specifically targets identifying a scientist and their invention/s. Coining a term is not an invention in the scientific/technological sense intended by the competency, so the card does not directly support the skill.

copy.en:
Who invented the word "dinosaur"?

The word "dinosaur" was coined by English scientist Richard Owen!
copy.tl:
Sino ang lumikha ng salitang "dinosaur"?

Ang salitang "dinosaur" ay nilikha ng siyentipikong Ingles na si Richard Owen!
copy.bis:
Kinsay naghimo sa pulong nga "dinosaur"?

Ang pulong nga "dinosaur" gimugna sa Ingles nga siyentista nga si Richard Owen!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Night is cooler and quieter, so animals like bats and owls find food more easily then and avoid the daytime heat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem

Why are bats and owls awake at night?

Night is cooler and quieter, so animals like bats and owls find food more easily then and avoid the daytime heat.

Mas malamig at tahimik sa gabi, kaya mas madali silang makahanap ng pagkain gaya ng paniki at kuwago, at naiiwasan nila ang init sa araw.

Mas bugnaw ug hilom sa gabii, mao nga mas sayon nila makaplagan ang pagkaon sama sa kabog ug ngiwngiw, ug malikayan ang init sa adlaw.

Why do some animals store food?

Kay naay mga panahon nga lisod mangita og pagkaon, sama sa bugnaw nga tingtugnaw — mao nga nagatipig sila alang sa unahan!

copy.bis: Mas init ang tubig-dagat duol sa equator ug mas bugnaw duol sa mga polo. Maong lahi ang kinabuhi sa dagat sa matag banda—sama sa warm-water corals sa tropics!

Why brush your teeth every day?

Bacteria in your mouth feed on sweet leftovers on your teeth and make an acid that damages them. Brushing every day removes these bacteria so your teeth don't get cavities.
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat magsipilyo araw-araw?

May bacteria sa bibig na kumakain ng matamis na natitira sa ngipin at gumagawa ng acid na sumisira dito. Ang pagsisipilyo araw-araw ay nag-aalis sa kanila para hindi mabubungbong ang ngipin.
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan magsipilyo adlaw-adlaw?

Adunay bacteria sa baba nga mokaon sa tam-is nga nahibilin sa ngipon ug maghimo og acid nga modaot niini. Ang adlaw-adlaw nga pagsipilyo makakuha niini aron dili mabongbong ang ngipon.

copy.tl: Tumatagal ng maraming taon ang de-latang pagkain! Iniinit ito nang husto para patayin ang germs, tapos selyado para walang bagong bakterya o hangin na makapasok.
copy.bis: Molungtad og daghang tuig ang de lata nga pagkaon! Gipainit pag-ayo aron patyon ang germs, dayon gisarado aron walay bag-ong bakterya o hangin nga makasulod.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ultraviolet and infrared but does not compare their wavelengths or frequencies, nor does it discuss other EM waves. It only explains eye sensitivity to a narrow range, which is not the competency's focus.

Why can't we see ultraviolet and infrared light?

Our eyes are only sensitive to a narrow range of light, so these invisible rays stay hidden!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi natin nakikita ang ultraviolet at infrared?

Ang ating mga mata ay sensitibo lamang sa makitid na saklaw ng liwanag, kaya nakatago ang mga ito!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili nato makita ang ultraviolet ug infrared?

Ang atong mata sensitibo lamang sa pig-ot nga sakop sa kahayag, mao nga nagpabilin silang tinago!

copy.en:
How does milk become cheese?

An acid or special enzyme makes it curdle, separating the solid part from the liquid to shape into cheese!
copy.tl:
Paano nagiging keso ang gatas?

Ang acid o espesyal na enzyme ay nagpapamuo nito, na naghihiwalay sa solidong bahagi mula sa likido para hubugin bilang keso!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa keso gikan sa gatas?

Ang acid o espesyal nga enzyme mopalamot niini, nga magbulag sa gahi nga bahin gikan sa likido aron himoon nga keso!

copy.en: A compass needle is a small magnet that lines up with Earth's magnetic field! That's why it always points toward magnetic north to help us find direction.
copy.tl: Ang karayom ng kompas ay isang maliit na magnet na pumapantay sa magnetic field ng Earth! Kaya palaging tumuturo ito sa magnetic north para matulungan tayong malaman ang direksyon.
copy.bis: Ang dagom sa compass usa ka gamayng magnet nga mopahiluna sa magnetic field sa Earth! Mao nga kanunay kining motudlo sa magnetic north aron makatabang nato mahibal-an ang direksyon.

copy.en:
Why is cooked food safer to eat than raw food?

The heat from cooking kills most bacteria and germs that can make you sick!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas ligtas kainin ang lutong pagkain kaysa hilaw?

Pinapatay ng init ng pagluluto ang karamihan ng bakterya at mikrobyo na pwedeng magkasakit sa'yo!
copy.bis:
Ngano mas luwas ang luto nga pagkaon kaysa hilaw?

Ang init sa pagluto mopatay sa kadaghanan sa bakterya ug mikrobyo nga makapasakit nimo!

copy.en:
Ever feel your ears pop when going up high? Why does that happen?

When you rise quickly in a plane or up a mountain, the air pressure drops because the air gets thinner. That pressure change is what makes your ears pop!
copy.tl:
Naramdaman mo na bang pumutok ang tenga mo pag-akyat sa mataas? Bakit iyon?

Kapag mabilis kang umaakyat sa eroplano o bundok, bumababa ang air pressure dahil nanipis ang hangin. Ang pagbabago ng pressure ang nagpuputok sa tenga mo!
copy.bis:
Nabati na ba nimo ang pagbutok sa dalunggan pag-akyat sa habog? Ngano man?

Kon paspas ka mosaka sa ayroplano o bukid, mokunhod ang air pressure kay nipis ang hangin. Ang kausaban sa pressure ang nagbutok sa imong dalunggan!

copy.bis: Nagsusi kita sa kawanangan aron magkat-on bahin sa ubang planeta, mahibaw-an ang pagsugod sa mga bituon, ug pangitaon ang kinabuhi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bacteria and mold grow on food and spoil it. Keeping food cold or dry slows them down

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions growth of bacteria and mold, but it does not teach the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a concept. Growth here is about spoilage, not a lesson on living-thing characteristics.

copy.en:
Why does food go bad?

Bacteria and mold grow on food and spoil it. Keeping food cold or dry slows them down — that's why we use the fridge!
copy.tl:
Bakit nasisira ang pagkain?

Sumisibol ang bakterya at amag sa pagkain kaya ito nabubulok. Pinapabagal sila ng lamig o pagpapatuyo — kaya natin ginagamit ang ref!
copy.bis:
Ngano madunot ang pagkaon?

Ang bakterya ug agup-op motubo sa pagkaon busa kini madunot. Mahinay sila kon bugnaw o uga — mao nga mogamit ta og ref!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bacteria move and multiply slower in the cold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion

copy.en: A fridge does not kill the germs that spoil food — it only slows them down! Bacteria move and multiply slower in the cold, so your food lasts longer.
copy.tl: Hindi pinapatay ng ref ang mikrobyo na nagpapabulok ng pagkain — pinapabagal lang nito sila! Mas mabagal kumilos at dumami ang bakterya kapag malamig, kaya mas tumatagal ang pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang ref dili mopatay sa mikrobyo nga maoy hinungdan sa pagkadunot sa pagkaon — gipahinay lang niini sila! Ang bakterya hinay molihok ug modaghan kung bugnaw, mao nga mas dugay ang pagkaon.

copy.en:
Why does fruit turn sweet when it ripens?

As fruit ripens, it gives off a gas called ethylene. This gas turns the fruit's starch into sugar, softens it, and changes its color -- that's why ripe fruit tastes sweet!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagiging matamis ang prutas kapag hinog na?

Habang nahihinog ang prutas, naglalabas ito ng gas na tinatawag na ethylene. Ginagawang asukal nito ang starch, pinalalambot ang laman, at binabago ang kulay -- kaya matamis ang hinog na prutas!
copy.bis:
Nganong mahimong tam-is ang prutas kon hinog na?

Samtang mahinog ang prutas, mobuga kini og gas nga gitawag ethylene. Ang gas mohimo sa starch nga asukar, mopahumok sa unod, ug mousab sa kolor -- mao nga tam-is ang hinog nga prutas!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a food-preservation example but does not explain factors affecting rates of chemical reactions, such as concentration, temperature, or surface area, nor does it connect the example to reaction rates.

Why does honey almost never spoil?

Honey has so much sugar and so little water that bacteria simply cannot survive inside it!
copy.tl:
Bakit halos hindi nabubulok ang pulot-pukyutan?

Sobrang dami ng asukal at napakakaunting tubig sa pulot-pukyutan, kaya hindi mabuhay ang bakterya sa loob nito!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang dugos halos dili madunot?

Sobra kaayo ang kalamay ug gamay ra kaayo ang tubig sa dugos, mao nga ang bakterya dili mabuhi sa sulod niini!

copy.en: Lemons and calamansi taste sour because they contain citric acid — a mild acid that our tongue senses as a sour flavor!
copy.tl: Maasim ang kalamansi at lemon dahil may citric acid sila — isang banayad na asido na nararamdaman ng dila natin bilang maasim na lasa!
copy.bis: Aslom ang kalamansi ug lemon tungod kay aduna silay citric acid — usa ka hinay nga asido nga mabati sa atong dila isip aslom nga lami!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is the moon covered in craters?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars

It is related to the moon but not directly to the competency's skill.

copy.en:
Why is the moon covered in craters?

Space rocks crash into the moon and make craters! Since the moon has no air or weather, the craters don't erode away — so they stay for a very long time!
copy.tl:
Bakit puno ng crater ang buwan?

Mga bato mula sa kalawakan ang bumabangga sa buwan! Dahil walang hangin o panahon sa buwan, hindi naaagnas ang mga crater — kaya nananatili ang mga ito nang napakatagal!
copy.bis:
Ngano puno og crater ang bulan?

Mga bato gikan sa kawanangan ang nagbangga sa bulan! Tungod kay walay hangin o panahon sa bulan, dili maguba o mawala ang mga crater — maong magpabilin kini og dugay kaayo!

copy.tl: Itinutulak pataas ng tubig ang lahat na nasa loob niyan—yan ang buoyancy! Lumulutang ang bagay kung mas magaan ito kaysa tubig na itinabi nito, at lumulubog kung mas mabigat.
copy.bis: Ang tubig motukmod pataas sa tanan nga anaa sulod niini—mao na ang buoyancy! Molutaw ang butang kung mas gaan kini kaysa tubig nga gisalikway niini, ug molunod kung mas bug-at.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By letting other birds raise its eggs, a brood parasite saves its own energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a specific reproductive strategy (brood parasitism) in birds, not the classification of animal groups by whether they give birth to live young or lay eggs. It does not address mammals, reptiles, or the general grouping required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why do brood parasites let others raise their eggs?

By letting other birds raise its eggs, a brood parasite saves its own energy — and can lay even more eggs!
copy.tl:
Bakit ipinapaalaga ng brood parasite ang itlog nito sa iba?

Sa pagpapaalaga ng itlog nito sa iba, nakakatipid ng lakas ang brood parasite — at nagagawa pa nitong mangitlog nang mas marami!
copy.bis:
Nganong gipaatiman sa brood parasite ang iyang itlog sa uban?

Pinaagi sa pagpaatiman sa iyang itlog sa uban, makatipig og kusog ang brood parasite — ug makahimo pa kini og daghang itlog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pure substance has the same properties everywhere!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a pure substance has uniform properties (taste, color, density), which is a general characteristic but does not address the competency's required specifics: fixed chemical composition, examples of elements and compounds, or the unique number of protons in an element's atoms. It only touches on uniformity, not the chemical composition or atomic-level details.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a mixture, parts can differ, so samples from different spots might not match.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card contrasts pure substances with mixtures by noting that mixture parts can differ, which is a basic distinction. However, the competency requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions. The card provides no examples of mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, and does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures in a way that directly supports the competency.

copy.en: A pure substance has the same properties everywhere! Every part has the same taste, color, and density. In a mixture, parts can differ, so samples from different spots might not match.
copy.tl: Ang purong sangkap ay parehong-pareho ang katangian saan ka man kumuha ng sample! Pareho ang lasa, kulay, at bigat. Pero sa mixture, puwedeng magkaiba ang bahagi, kaya hindi laging pareho ang sample.
copy.bis: Ang putli nga sustansya parehas gyud ang kinaiya bisan asa ka mokuha og sample! Parehas ang lami, kolor, ug gibug-aton. Apan sa mixture, mahimong magkalahi ang mga bahin, busa ang sample mahimong dili pareho.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Since there is no air in space, rockets carry their own oxygen to burn fuel
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen as a component of air but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It focuses on rockets needing oxygen for combustion, not on the composition of air.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rockets carry their own oxygen to burn fuel
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves burning fuel with oxygen, but it does not describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, such as burning wood or coal. It is about combustion in space, not about temperature-induced material changes.

copy.en: Since there is no air in space, rockets carry their own oxygen to burn fuel and fly beyond the atmosphere!
copy.tl: Dahil walang hangin sa kalawakan, nagdadala ang mga rocket ng sarili nilang oxygen para masunog ang fuel at makalipad!
copy.bis: Tungod kay walay hangin sa kawanangan, magdala ang mga rocket ug kaugalingong oxygen para masunog ang fuel ug makalupad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electricity cannot pass easily through rubber, making it a great insulator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that rubber is an insulator and mentions its use in wire wrapping and gloves, but it does not teach designing or constructing a simple circuit, nor does it describe using a circuit to test and identify conducting and non-conducting materials. The content is related to the conductors/insulators topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's required investigation.

copy.en: Electricity cannot pass easily through rubber, making it a great insulator! That is why rubber wraps electrical wires and is used in electricians' gloves to prevent shocks.
copy.tl: Hindi madaling dumaan ang kuryente sa goma, kaya magandang insulator ito! Kaya binabalot ng goma ang mga kable at ginagamit sa electricians' gloves para iwas kuryente.
copy.bis: Dili dali moagi ang kuryente sa goma, maong maayo kini nga insulator! Mao nga giputos sa goma ang mga kable ug gigamit sa electricians' gloves aron malikayan ang kuryente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It comes from the rubber tree!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about useful things made from non-living materials. The card explicitly states natural rubber comes from a living tree's sap, which is a living material, not a non-living material. It does not support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: stretchy rubber
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card mentions 'stretchy rubber' but does not describe the property itself or teach how to identify/describe physical properties. It only uses the word 'stretchy' incidentally, so it is related vocabulary but not direct instructional support.

copy.en:
Where does natural rubber come from?

It comes from the rubber tree! People tap the tree to collect its milky white sap called latex, then dry and process it into stretchy rubber.
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang likas na goma?

Sa puno ng goma! Kinakatasan ng tao ang puting dagta nito na tinatawag na latex, tapos pinapatuyo at pinoproseso para maging stretchy na goma.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang natural nga goma?

Sa kahoy nga rubber tree! Taguson sa tawo ang puti niini nga dagta nga gitawag og latex, unya pagahon ug i-proseso aron mahimong stretchy nga goma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a layer of warm air sits on top of cooler air below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air temperature as part of a temperature inversion, but it does not identify or describe basic weather characteristics (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, etc.) as a topic. The focus is on smog trapping, not on weather descriptors.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: stopping dirty air from rising and clearing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on an environmental concern (smog) but does not identify local community issues or how science addresses them, such as waste treatment. It explains a physical mechanism rather than a community concern or scientific solution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a layer of warm air sits on top of cooler air below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a temperature inversion, not observing/recording weather changes or describing weather types/patterns. It does not support the skill of observing and recording weather over time.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a layer of warm air sits on top of cooler air below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a temperature inversion trapping smog, but it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. The warm air layer is not linked to solar energy or atmospheric interaction in the card text.

copy.en:
Why does smog get trapped over the city?

Smog gets worse when a layer of warm air sits on top of cooler air below! It acts like a lid, stopping dirty air from rising and clearing.
copy.tl:
Bakit naipon ang smog sa ibabaw ng lungsod?

Lumalala ang smog kapag ang mainit na hangin ay nakapatong sa malamig na hangin sa ibaba! Para itong takip na pumipigil sa maruming hangin na umakyat at kumalat.
copy.bis:
Nganong magtapok ang smog sa ibabaw sa siyudad?

Mograbe ang smog kung ang init nga hangin magpatong sa bugnaw nga hangin sa ubos! Sama kini sa taklob nga makapugong sa hugaw nga hangin sa pagsaka ug pagkatag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the temperature inside the main body cavity is too warm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in the weather can affect daily activities and explain how some types of weather can be dangerous for people
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why testes are outside the body due to temperature for sperm development. It has no content about weather changes affecting daily activities or dangerous weather.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the temperature inside the main body cavity is too warm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about human reproductive anatomy, not observing or recording weather changes or describing weather types and patterns.

copy.en: Why do the testes protrude outside the body?\n\nBecause the temperature inside the main body cavity is too warm and not suitable for the development of sperm cells!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakalabas sa katawan ang testes?

Dahil ang temperatura sa loob ng pangunahing bahagi ng katawan ay masyadong mainit at hindi angkop sa pagbuo ng sperm cells!
copy.bis:
Ngano nagawas man sa lawas ang testes?

Tungod kay ang temperatura sa sulod sa pangunang bahin sa lawas init kaayo ug dili angay sa pagtubo sa sperm cells!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the cornea, the front of the eye, needs air to focus light; water cancels that out
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains an everyday visual phenomenon involving light focusing, which is conceptually related to refraction, but it does not describe or illustrate reflection or refraction using mirrors, transparent blocks, lenses, or prisms, nor does it involve guided investigations as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the cornea, the front of the eye, needs air to focus light; water cancels that out
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card concerns vision and light focusing, which is broadly related to light energy, but it does not identify sources or uses of light, sound, or heat energy at school, home, or in the community as the competency requires.

copy.en:
Why does everything look blurry underwater?

It's blurry because the cornea, the front of the eye, needs air to focus light; water cancels that out — which is why goggles make things clear again.
copy.tl:
Bakit malabo ang tingin natin sa ilalim ng tubig?

Malabo dahil ang cornea, ang harap ng mata, ay umaasa sa hangin para maiangat ang focus; pinapawi ito ng tubig — kaya kailangan ng goggles para lumiwanag ulit.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga hanap ang atong panan-aw ilawom sa tubig?

Hanap kay ang cornea, ang atubangan sa mata, nagkinahanglan og hangin aron mo-focus; gipapas kini sa tubig — mao nga kinahanglan ang goggles aron klaro pag-usab.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Two ears let your brain compare when a sound reaches each side — that's how you know which direction a sound came from!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains sound localization (direction detection) using two ears, which is about hearing perception, not about how sound is made or transferred. The competency focuses on sound production and transfer in everyday situations; the card does not address those aspects.

copy.en:
Why do we have two ears?

Two ears let your brain compare when a sound reaches each side — that's how you know which direction a sound came from!
copy.tl:
Bakit dalawa ang tainga natin?

Ang dalawang tainga ay nagpapahintulot sa utak na ikumpara kung kailan umabot ang tunog sa bawat gilid — kaya nalalaman natin kung saan nanggaling ang tunog!
copy.bis:
Nganong duha ang atong dalunggan?

Ang duha ka dalunggan magtugot sa utok nga itandi kanus-a moabot ang tingog sa matag kilid — mao nga mahibal-an nato kon asa naggikan ang tingog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is too acidic for most spoilage bacteria to survive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses food preservation via acidity but does not explain any factor affecting the rate of a chemical reaction (e.g., concentration, temperature, surface area). It only states that acidity prevents bacterial growth, which is not about reaction rates.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is too acidic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions vinegar as acidic but does not identify it as a solution, nor does it discuss litmus indicator reactions or classification as acid/base/salt. It only uses acidity as a preservation mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vinegar is too acidic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions vinegar's acidity but does not identify common acids, bases, or salts using indicators. It does not name vinegar as an acid or provide any indicator-based identification.

copy.en:
Why do pickled vegetables and vinegar-soaked foods last so long?

Vinegar is too acidic for most spoilage bacteria to survive — so the food stays fresh longer!
copy.tl:
Bakit tumatagal ang atsara at mga pagkaing binabad sa suka?

Masyadong maasim ang suka para mabuhay ang karamihan ng bakterya na nagpapabulok — kaya tumatagal ang pagkain!
copy.bis:
Ngano molungtad og dugay ang atsara ug mga pagkaong gibabad sa suka?

Aslom kaayo ang suka aron mabuhi ang kadaghanan sa bakterya nga nagpapabulok — kay molungtad ang pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wild forest bananas are packed with small, hard seeds, making them hard to eat—unlike the soft, seedless bananas we buy at market
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Hard seeds vs seedless market fruit is food/culinary contrast, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

copy.en: Wild forest bananas are packed with small, hard seeds, making them hard to eat—unlike the soft, seedless bananas we buy at market.
copy.tl: Puno ng maliliit at matitigas na buto ang ligaw na saging sa gubat kaya mahirap kainin—hindi tulad ng saging sa palengke na halos walang buto.
copy.bis: Puno sa gagmay ug gahi nga liso ang ligaw nga saging sa lasang mao nga lisod kaonon—dili sama sa saging sa merkado nga halos walay liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its soft leaves and shoots are cooked as a tasty vegetable.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves and stems (climbing vine, red/purple stems) but does not describe their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only describes appearance and use as food, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Alugbati is a climbing vine that crawls up fences and trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the shoot system (vine, stems) but does not describe the root system or explain why these systems are important. No functional explanation is given, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Alugbati is a climbing vine that crawls up fences and trees — some have red or purple stems! Its soft leaves and shoots are cooked as a tasty vegetable.
copy.tl: Ang alugbati ay isang baging na gumagapang at umaakyat sa bakod at puno — may mga uri nito na pula o lila ang tangkay! Niluluto ang malambot nitong dahon at usbong bilang masarap na gulay.
copy.bis: Ang alugbati usa ka baging nga mokatay ug mosaka sa koral ug kahoy — adunay matang niini nga pula o lila ang tangkay! Lutoon ang humok nga dahon ug salingsing niini isip lami nga utanon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: edible shoots and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves and shoots but only as food gathered by people; it does not describe observing outer plant parts or their role in absorbing water and nutrients from the soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: edible shoots and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions shoots but not the root system, and does not explain the importance of the root and shoot systems for plant function; it only notes that shoots and leaves are eaten.

copy.en: Besides pako, Filipinos gather and eat many other wild greens, like edible shoots and leaves.
copy.tl: Bukod sa pako, marami pang ligaw na gulay ang pinupulot at kinakain ng mga Pilipino tulad ng talbos at dahon.
copy.bis: Gawas sa pako, daghan pang ihalas nga utanon ang gipuniton ug gikaon sa mga Pilipino sama sa talbos ug dahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some plants people call weeds, like kulitis and talinum, are actually nutritious vegetables people eat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that people eat certain weeds, which is an example of humans using plants for food, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It only states a fact about edibility, not the dependency relationship.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: are actually nutritious vegetables people eat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on food as something people get from plants, but it does not identify the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) or teach that these are needs. It is about a misconception regarding weeds, not about basic needs.

copy.en:
Are all weeds useless?

No! Some plants people call weeds, like kulitis and talinum, are actually nutritious vegetables people eat. Not every wild plant is trash.
copy.tl:
Wala bang silbi ang lahat ng damo?

Hindi! Ang ilang tinatawag na damo, tulad ng kulitis at talinum, ay masustansyang gulay na kinakain. Hindi lahat ng ligaw na halaman ay basura.
copy.bis:
Walay pulos ba ang tanang sagbot?

Dili! Ang uban giilang sagbot, sama sa kulitis ug talinum, mao ang masustansya nga utanon nga gikaon. Dili tanang ihalas nga tanom basura.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: stand the stems in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stems but does not teach the outer parts of plants or their role in taking up water and nutrients from the soil. It is about water loss after picking, not plant part functions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: lose water quickly after picking
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses water loss in wild greens, but does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It is not instructional for this competency.

copy.en:
Why do wild greens wilt so fast?

Wild greens lose water quickly after picking, so cook them right away or stand the stems in water — they won't keep in the fridge like regular vegetables.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabilis malanta ang gulay-ligaw?

Mabilis nawawalan ng tubig ang gulay-ligaw pagkatapos pitasin, kaya lutuin agad o ibabad ang tangkay sa tubig — hindi ito tatagal sa ref gaya ng ibang gulay.
copy.bis:
Ngano paspas malaya ang gulay-ligaw?

Paspas mawad-an og tubig ang gulay-ligaw human pupua, mao nga lutoa dayon o ibutang ang tangkay sa tubig — dili kini molungtad sa ref sama sa ubang utanon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helping keep their genetic diversity healthy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions genetic diversity, a component of biodiversity, but does not explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining ecosystem stability during difficult conditions such as food shortages, disease, or climate change. It only describes a conservation tool (wildlife corridors) and its effect on genetic diversity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: lets animals move between separated forests
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes movement between habitats, which is an interaction between living things and the environment, but it does not explain how interactions bring good or harm to the living things involved. It does not address the cause-effect relationship of interactions on organisms' well-being.

copy.en: A wildlife corridor is a strip of connected habitat that lets animals move between separated forests, helping keep their genetic diversity healthy.
copy.tl: Ang wildlife corridor ay pagdurugtong ng mga kagubatan na nagbibigay-daan sa mga hayop na makakilos sa magkahiwalay na tirahan, tumutulong ito sa kanilang genetic diversity.
copy.bis: Ang wildlife corridor usa ka konektadong bahin sa habitat nga nagtugot sa mga mananap nga mobalhin taliwala sa nahimulag nga lugar, nagtabang kini sa ilang genetic diversity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hurt or captured animals are nursed back to health first, then set free again into their natural home
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the process of wildlife rescue (nursing and releasing animals) but does not teach the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. It is about individual animal care, not environmental protection or conservation rationale.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hurt or captured animals are nursed back to health first, then set free again into their natural home
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to research how to protect and conserve endangered and/or economically important species in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires researching how to protect and conserve endangered/economically important species in the local community using secondary sources. The card only states a general definition of wildlife rescue; it does not address endangered species, local community, or research-based conservation methods.

copy.en: In wildlife rescue, hurt or captured animals are nursed back to health first, then set free again into their natural home.
copy.tl: Sa wildlife rescue, ang nasaktang o nahuling hayop ay pinapagaling muna bago pakawalan pabalik sa kanilang likas na tirahan.
copy.bis: Sa wildlife rescue, ang nasamdan o nadakpan nga hayop pagaayohon una una buhian balik sa ilang natural nga puy-anan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind is the main force that pushes and drives surface ocean currents
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an ocean current (Kuroshio Current), which is a body of water, but the competency requires identifying local examples of landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines and describing their influence on living/non-living components. The card does not identify local examples nor describe influence; it only states that wind drives surface currents.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind is the main force that pushes and drives surface ocean currents
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about exploring and demonstrating ways to make objects move by natural causes such as wind and water, or by people. The card mentions wind as a force moving ocean currents, but it does not explore or demonstrate movement of objects in a guided activity; it is a factual statement about ocean currents, not an exploration of moving objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind is the main force that pushes and drives surface ocean currents
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out simple investigations to demonstrate that contact forces cause objects to move in the same direction as the direction that the force is applied
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires carrying out simple investigations to demonstrate that contact forces cause objects to move in the same direction as the force applied. The card states that wind pushes surface currents, but wind is a non-contact force, not a contact force, and there is no investigation or demonstration of force direction. The content is only tangentially related to forces causing motion.

copy.en: Wind is the main force that pushes and drives surface ocean currents, like the famous Kuroshio Current!
copy.tl: Ang hangin ang pangunahing lakas na nagpapagalaw at nagtutulak sa mga agos sa ibabaw ng karagatan tulad ng Kuroshio Current!
copy.bis: Ang hangin mao ang nag-unang kusog nga nagpadagan sa mga sulog sa ibabaw sa dagat sama sa Kuroshio Current!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind energy comes from the powerful force of blowing wind all around us!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that wind energy comes from blowing wind. It does not describe kinetic energy as movement of objects/particles or potential energy as stored energy due to position, so it does not directly support G8-F-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind energy comes from the powerful force of blowing wind all around us!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wind as a force but does not explore or demonstrate ways to make objects move by wind, water, pushing, pulling, rolling, or carrying. It only identifies wind as an energy source, not the movement of objects.

copy.en: Wind energy comes from the powerful force of blowing wind all around us!
copy.tl: Ang wind energy ay nagmumula sa lakas ng umiihip na hangin sa paligid natin!
copy.bis: Ang wind energy gikan sa kusog sa naghuros nga hangin sa palibot natong tanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind erosion is super slow — it can take hundreds or thousands of years to reshape the land.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the rate of wind erosion and corrects a misconception, but it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. It provides no mechanism, movement, or deposition of materials, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Can one strong wind blow away a whole mountain?

Nope! Wind erosion is super slow — it can take hundreds or thousands of years to reshape the land. Only a tiny bit is removed with each gust of wind.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang iisang malakas na hangin ang magpawala ng buong bundok?

Hindi! Napakabagal ng wind erosion — maaaring tumagal ng daan-daang o libo-libong taon bago mabago ang lupa. Konting butil lang ang naaalis sa bawat hangin.
copy.bis:
Makaya ba sa usa ka kusog nga hangin nga pukawon ang tibuok bukid?

Dili! Hinay kaayo ang wind erosion — moabot og gatusan o liboan ka tuig una mausab ang yuta. Gamay ra ang makuha matag hangin.

Ang friction mula sa mga puno, gusali, at ibabaw ay nagpapabagal ng hangin malapit sa lupa — pero mas mabilis ang hangin sa itaas kung saan mas kaunti ang friction!

Why do solar and wind energy need batteries?

Because they're not always available! There's no sun at night, and sometimes the wind is still. Batteries store extra energy so we can use it later.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng batteries ang solar at wind energy?

Dahil hindi sila palaging available! Walang araw sa gabi, at minsan tahimik ang hangin. Nag-iimbak ang batteries ng sobrang enerhiya para magamit natin mamaya.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga gikinahanglan sa solar ug wind energy ang mga baterya?

Tungod kay dili sila kanunay anaa! Walay adlaw sa gabii, ug usahay hilom ang hangin. Nagtipig ang mga baterya ug sobra nga enerhiya aron magamit nato unya.

Why does wind direction matter for weather?

Wind from the southwest (habagat) brings rain, while wind from the northeast (amihan) brings dry weather!

Bakit importante ang direksyon ng hangin sa panahon?

Ang hangin mula sa timog-kanluran (habagat) ay nagdadala ng ulan, habang ang hangin mula sa hilagang-silangan (amihan) ay nagdadala ng tuyong panahon!

Ngano importante ang direksyon sa hangin sa panahon?

Ang hangin gikan sa habagatan-kasadpan (habagat) nagdala og ulan, samtang ang hangin gikan sa amihanan-sidlakan (amihan) nagdala og tuyot nga panahon!

Ang mga punong itinatanim bilang windbreak ay nagpoprotekta ng mga tanaman mula sa matinding hangin, nagpapababa ng erosion, at nagtutulong na mapanatili ang kahalumigmigan ng lupa!
copy.bis:

Ang mga puno nga itinanom isip windbreak nagpanalipod sa mga pananim gikan sa kusog nga hangin, nagpababa sa erosion, ug nagtabang sa pagpatagan sa kahalumigmigan sa yuta!

Where does our firewood come from?

Firewood used as fuel comes from the branches and trunks of trees!
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang ating panggatong na kahoy?

Ang panggatong na kahoy ay galing sa mga sanga at katawan ng mga puno!
copy.bis:
Asalinhagikan ang atong kahoy nga sugnod?

Ang kahoy nga sugnod naggikan sa mga sanga ug lawas sa mga kahoy!

Why does a woodpecker drum on wood?

Woodpeckers don't peck only to find food — they also drum fast on wood to send signals to other birds.

Hindi lang para sa pagkain ang pagkatok ng woodpecker — gumagamit din ito ng mabilis na pagtambol para magpadala ng senyas sa ibang ibon.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagatuktok sa kahoy ang woodpecker?

Dili lang para sa pagkaon ang pagtuktok sa woodpecker — mogamit usab kini og paspas nga pagtambol aron magpadala og senyas sa ubang langgam.

Why does wool keep us so warm?

Wool has curly fibers that trap tiny pockets of air! Those trapped air pockets slow down the heat leaving your body, keeping you cozy and warm.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo pinapanatiling mainit ng wool?

Ang wool ay may kulot na hibla na nagkukulong ng maliliit na bulsa ng hangin! Ang mga nakukulong na hangin ay pumipigil sa pagtakas ng init ng katawan, kaya nananatili kang mainit.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang wool makapainit kanato?

Ang wool adunay kulot nga mga hibla nga mokulong ug gagmay nga mga bulsa sa hangin! Kana nga nakulong nga hangin makapahinay sa paggawas sa kainit gikan sa lawas, nagpabilin kang komportable.

Ever wonder why sheep's wool keeps you so warm?

Wool is a natural protein fiber made of keratin! Its crimped fibers trap air, making it an excellent insulator to keep your body warm.

Alam mo ba kung bakit nakakapagpainit ang balahibo ng karnero?

Ang lana ay isang natural na protein fiber na gawa sa keratin! Nakakabitag ito ng hangin sa mga hibla nito, kaya napakagandang insulator para sa init ng katawan.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nganinit ang lana gikan sa karnero?

Ang lana usa ka natural nga protein fiber nga gihimo sa keratin! Nagbitad kini og hangin tali sa crimped fibers, naghimo niini nga maayong insulator nga nagpadayon sa init sa lawas.

How do worker ants find their way home?

A worker ant never gets lost going home! It follows the scent it left on the path, and also uses the sun's position and nearby landmarks to find its way back.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakauwi ang worker ant?

Hindi naliligaw ang worker ant pabalik sa pugad! Sinusundan nito ang amoy na iniwan sa daan, at ginagamit din ang posisyon ng araw at mga palatandaan sa paligid para makauwi.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpauli sa worker ant?

Dili masaag ang worker ant pabalik sa salag! Sundon niini ang baho nga gibilin sa dalan, ug gamiton usab ang posisyon sa adlaw ug mga ilhanan sa palibot aron makabalik.

Why do ants walk in a line?

When a worker ant finds food, it leaves a special scent along the path. Other ants follow that scent, which is why we see them marching one after another in a line.
copy.tl:
Bakit sunud-sunod lumalakad ang mga langgam?

Kapag may nahanap na pagkain ang isang worker ant, nag-iiwan ito ng espesyal na amoy sa daanan. Sinusundan ng ibang langgam ang amoy na iyon, kaya nakikita natin silang naglalakad nang sunud-sunod.
copy.bis:
Ngano nagsunod-sunod paglakaw ang mga langgam?

Kon makakita og pagkaon ang usa ka worker ant, magbilin kini og espesyal nga baho sa agianan. Ang ubang langgam mosunod niini nga baho, mao nga makita nato sila nga naglakaw nga sunod-sunod.

Can humans regrow a lost finger?

Kaya ng tao gumaling ng sugat at bumuo ng bagong balat, pero hindi na kayang patubuin muli ang buong bahaging nawala gaya ng daliri. Ang ibang hayop naman, gaya ng butiki, kaya pa nga patubuin ang naputol na buntot!

Makaayo ang tawo og samad ug makahimo og bag-ong panit, apan dili na makapatubo pag-usab og tibuok bahin nga nawala sama sa tudlo. Ang ubang hayop, sama sa tiki, makapatubo pa gani sa naputol nga buntot!
